A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the estrous cycle does not appear to be a major factor influencing the acquisition or maintenance of operant responding for 10% alcohol in female Wistar rats, but may be a factor in the amount of intake during limited access to ethanol.
the effects of the estrous phase are not always present, and that the estrous cycle may not be an important factor in the control of alcohol self-administration in all female rats.
ethanol self-administration may be more sensitive to the estrous cycle when cycles are synchronized, and that estrus is the least reinforcing phase of the cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the estrous cycle can have a significant impact on the behavior of female rats.
